He played [[college basketball]] for the [[UNLV Runnin' Rebels basketball|UNLV Runnin' Rebels]], [[Florida Gulf Coast Eagles men's basketball|Florida Gulf Coast Eagles]] and [[Morgan State Bears men's basketball|Morgan State Bears]]. ==High school career== Baxter attended Oldsmar Christian School in [[Oldsmar, Florida]]. He saw his stock rise as he played for Team Breakdown in the Under Armour Association in 2015. Baxter committed to play [[college basketball]] for the [[South Florida Bulls men's basketball|South Florida Bulls]] on May 1, 2015.{{cite web |last1=Phillips |first1=Scott |title=South Florida lands top-150 Class of 2016 wing |url=https://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2015/05/01/south-florida-lands-class-of-2016-wing-troy-baxter/ |website=NBC Sports |access-date=October 20, 2021 |date=May 1, 2015}} Baxter averaged 17 points, 7 rebounds and 1.5 blocks as a senior during the 2015–16 season.{{cite web |last1=Knight |first1=Joey |title=Heralded freshman Troy Baxter won't join USF |url=https://www.tampabay.com/heralded-freshman-troy-baxter-wont-join-usf/2291111/ |website=Tampa Bay Times |access-date=October 20, 2021 |date=August 27, 2016}} He was rated as a four-star recruit and ranked 90th in the [[ESPN]] 100. Baxter won the 2016 American Family Insurance High School Slam Dunk Contest.{{cite web |title=South Florida signee Troy Baxter wins dunk contest at High School Slam |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2016/south-florida-signee-troy-baxter-wins-dunk-contest-at-high-school-slam |website=USA Today High School Sports |access-date=October 20, 2021 |date=April 1, 2016}} On August 27, 2016, it was reported that Baxter had been released from his [[National Letter of Intent|letter of intent]] with South Florida. On September 1, 2016, he committed to the [[UNLV Runnin' Rebels basketball|UNLV Runnin' Rebels]].{{cite web |last1=Bern |first1=Taylor |title=Four-star forward joins UNLV’s 2016 recruiting class |url=https://lasvegassun.com/news/2016/sep/01/four-star-forward-joins-this-years-recruiting-clas/ |website=Las Vegas Sun |access-date=October 20, 2021 |date=September 1, 2016}} ==College career== ===UNLV (2016–2017)=== Baxter averaged 4.3 points and 2.3 rebounds per game during his freshman season with the UNLV Runnin' Rebels.{{cite web |title=Troy Baxter Jr., Zion Morgan, Jalen Poyser leaving UNLV after 1 season |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/19034384/troy-baxter-jr-zion-morgan-jalen-poyser-leaving-unlv-rebels-1-season |website=ESPN |access-date=October 20, 2021 |date=March 30, 2017}} His playing time did not meet his expectations and the Runnin' Rebels only won four games in conference play. On March 30, 2017, Baxter announced that he would not return to the Runnin' Rebels. ===Florida Gulf Coast (2017–2019)=== On June 20, 2017, Baxter committed to play for the [[Florida Gulf Coast Eagles men's basketball|Florida Gulf Coast Eagles]].{{cite web |last1=Caldwell |first1=Dana |title=FGCU men add UNLV sophomore forward Troy Baxter with last scholarship |url=https://www.naplesnews.com/story/sports/college/fgcu/2017/06/21/fgcu-men-add-unlv-sophomore-forward-troy-baxter-last-scholarship/413059001/ |website=Naples Daily News |access-date=October 20, 2021 |date=June 21, 2017}} He had to sit out the 2017–18 due to [[National Collegiate Athletic Association]] (NCAA) transfer rules. Baxter treated practice sessions as his game time and credits the period with helping him develop a better feel for basketball. Baxter averaged 7.5 points, 2.9 rebounds, 1.1 assists and 1.1 blocks per game during the 2018–19 season. On April 5, 2019, he declared for the [[2019 NBA draft]].{{cite web |title=FGCU’s Baxter declares for NBA Draft |url=https://fgcuathletics.com/news/2019/4/5/mens-basketball-fgcus-baxter-declares-for-nba-draft.aspx |website=FGCU Athletics |access-date=October 20, 2021 |date=April 5, 2019}} He did not sign with an agent and was eligible to return to college.{{cite web |last1=Hardwig |first1=Greg |title=College basketball: FGCU's Troy Baxter declares for NBA Draft; Scott, Ernst at new schools |url=https://www.naplesnews.com/story/sports/college/fgcu/2019/04/05/fgcu-mens-basketballs-troy-baxter-declares-nba-draft/3377411002/ |website=Naples Daily News |access-date=October 20, 2021 |date=April 5, 2019}} Baxter elected to return after not liking his draft chances but announced his intention to transfer. ===Morgan State (2019–2021)=== Baxter desired to transfer to a team with coaches that had experience sending players to the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He chose the [[Morgan State Bears men's basketball|Morgan State Bears]] for their head coach [[Kevin Broadus]] who had coached 12 future NBA players during his college career. Baxter averaged 10.2 points and 5.1 rebounds per game during the 2019–20 season. His 1.9 blocks per game were the second highest in the [[Mid-Eastern Athletic Conference]] (MEAC). Baxter averaged 15.5 points, 4.4 rebounds and 1.6 blocks per game during the 2020–21 season.{{cite web |last1=Davies |first1=Spencer |title=Troy Baxter Jr. had to learn to fall in love with the grind |url=https://www.basketballnews.com/stories/troy-baxter-jr-had-to-learn-to-fall-in-love-with-the-grind-nba-draft-prospects-2021 |website=Basketball News |access-date=October 20, 2021 |date=July 30, 2021}} He was selected to the All-MEAC First Team and the All-Defensive Team.{{cite web |title=MEAC Announces Men's Basketball All-Conference Honors, presented by TowneBank |url=https://meacsports.com/news/2021/3/5/meac-announces-mens-basketball-all-conference-honors-presented-by-townebank.aspx |website=Mid-Eastern Athletic Conference |access-date=October 20, 2021 |date=March 5, 2021}} He won the 2021 Great Clips Slam Dunk Championship and became the first player to win slam dunk titles in high school and college.{{cite web |last1=Sharrock |first1=Rory |title=Tallahassee native Troy Baxter Jr. leaps over foes as NCAA slam dunk champion |url=https://www.tallahassee.com/story/sports/2021/04/06/tallahassee-native-troy-baxter-jr-soars-ncaa-slam-dunk-champion/7084169002/ |website=Tallahassee Democrat |access-date=October 20, 2021 |date=April 6, 2021}} On August 9, 2021, Baxter was named as the MEAC Male Student-Athlete of the Year for his academic and extracurricular work.{{cite web |title=MEAC Names Troy Baxter, Jr. 2021 Male Student-Athlete of the Year |url=https://meacsports.com/news/2021/8/9/mens-basketball-meac-names-troy-baxter-jr-2021-male-student-athlete-of-the-year.aspx |website=Mid-Eastern Athletic Conference League]].{{cite web|first=Rob|last=Schaefer|title=Bulls' Summer League roster headlined by Patrick Williams|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/chicago/bulls/bulls-2021-summer-league-roster-headlined-patrick-williams|website=NBC Sports Chicago|date=August 4, 2021|access-date=October 23, 2021}} On October 2021|access-date=October 23, 2021}} but was waived the next day.{{cite tweet|author=Chicago Bulls|number=1449423925004361728|title=Transactions: We have waived forwards Stanley Johnson and Troy Baxter Jr.|user=chicagobulls|date=October 16, 2021|access-date=October 23, 2021}}{{cite web|first=K. C.|last=Johnson|title=Bulls waive Stanley Johnson, keep Matt Thomas|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/chicago/bulls/bulls-waive-stanley-johnson-keep-shooting-matt-thomas?cid=Yahoo&partner=ya4nbcs|website=NBC Sports Chicago|date=October 17, 2021|access-date=October 20, 2021}} Baxter joined the [[Windy City Bulls]] of the [[NBA G League]] as an affiliate player.{{cite web |last1=Brown |first1=Kyle |title=Windy City Bulls Announce Opening Night Roster |url=https://windycity.gleague.nba.com/news/windy-city-bulls-finalize-training-camp-roster-announce-basketball-operations-staff/ |website=NBA.com |access-date=November 7, 2021 |date=October 25, 2021}} He was waived by Windy City on February 1, 2022. He was then acquired by the [[Wisconsin Herd]] on February 2; waived on February 6; acquired by the [[Grand Rapids Gold]] on February 14; waived on March 3; and then acquired by the [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]] on March 18.{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2021-22 NBA G League Transactions|date=February 7, 2022|access-date=February 7, 2022}} In May and June 2022, Baxter played eight games for [[Indios de San Francisco de Macorís|Indios de San Francisco]] of the Dominican [[Liga Nacional de Baloncesto]] (LNB).{{cite web|first=Hecmary|last=Ugarte|title=Troy Baxter Jr reforzará a los Indios de San Francisco|url=https://record.acento.com.do/baloncesto/troy-baxter-jr-reforzara-a-los-indios-de-san-francisco-48032|work=Récord|date=April 28, 2022|access-date=June 4, 2022|language=Spanish}}{{cite web|url=https://basketball.australiabasket.com/player/Troy-Baxter-Jr/413409|title=Troy Baxter Jr.|website=AustraliaBasket.com|access-date=April 4, 2023|url-access=subscription}} In October 2022, Baxter had a three-game stint with [[Deportivo San José]] of the [[Liga Sudamericana de Básquetbol]] during the [[2022 Liga Sudamericana de Básquetbol|2022 season]].{{cite web|title=Troy BAXTER JR|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/ligasudamericana/2022/player/TROY-BAXTER-JR|website=FIBA.basketball|access-date=October 24, 2022}} In November and December 2022, he had a four-game stint in Lebanon with [[Antranik Youth Association (basketball)|Antranik]]. He then moved to Mongolia in January 2023 to play for Khatsaga. On April 4, 2023, Baxter signed with the [[Canterbury Rams]] for the [[2023 New Zealand NBL season]].{{cite web|title=Import Alert!!! Baxter joined the [[Manawatu Jets]] for the [[2024 New Zealand NBL season]].{{cite web|title=2024 PLAYER ANNOUNCEMENT|url=https://www.facebook.com/jetsbasketballnz/posts/pfbid0J1hs51KubqcZ7BGW92GhsPBGXX3ujRidE6NCr7L8C3YGunP226yCFTK7JzkzHuQkl|website=Facebook.com/jetsbasketballnz|date=March 9, 2024|access-date=March 9, 2024}} He was released by the Jets on May 15, 2024.{{cite web|title=We've released import forward Troy Baxter Jr. from his 2024 New Zealand National Basketball League contract.|url=https://www.facebook.com/jetsbasketballnz/posts/pfbid02Ho5LfUE1m23q8b9hT7Hbu7NEbGK7FFs2GMrpn15pexLuK3p6CbHWFLpFsKvemCWol|website=Facebook.com/jetsbasketballnz|date=May 15, 2024|access-date=May 18, 2024}} On May 28, 2024, Baxter signed with the [[Calgary Surge]] of the [[Canadian Elite Basketball League]],{{cite web|title=Calgary Surge Sign Florida Forward Troy Baxtor Jr.|url=https://www.cebl.ca/calgary-surge-sign-florida-forward-troy-baxter-jr|website=cebl.ca|date=May 28, 2024|access-date=May 28, 2024}} but was waived on June 5. Baxter signed with the [[San Miguel Beermen]] for the [[2024–25 PBA Commissioner's Cup]] but was released without playing a game because he could not receive clearance.{{cite web |title=Miller subs as SMB import after Baxter fails to secure clearance |url=https://www.spin.ph/basketball/pba/miller-subs-in-as-smb-import-as-baxter-fails-to-secure-playing-clearance-a793-20241203 |website=Spin.ph |access-date=December 29, 2025 |date=December 3, 2024}} On February 5, 2025, Baxter signed with the [[Orthodox Club|Orthodox]] of the [[Jordanian Premier Basketball League]],{{cite web |title=Orthodox signs Troy Baxter Jr. |url=https://www.asia-basket.com/Jordan/news/915982/Orthodox-signs-Troy-Baxter-Jr |website=Eurobasket.com |access-date=February 5, 2025 |format=February 5, 2025}} but did not appear in a game. On February 20, he signed with the [[Amman United]] of the Jordanian Premier Basketball League.{{cite web |title=Amman United inks Troy Baxter Jr |url=https://www.asia-basket.com/Jordan/news/918573/Amman-United-inks-Troy-Baxter-Jr |website=Eurobasket.com |access-date=March 10, 2025 |date=February 20, 2025}} Baxter played seven games with Nadim Souaid Academy of the [[Lebanese Basketball League]] in 2025.{{cite web |last1=Abduljalil |first1=Yusuf |title=Al Ahly Tripoli lands Troy Baxter Jr., ex NSA |url=https://www.asia-basket.com/Lebanon/news/929406/Al-Ahly-Tripoli-lands-Troy-Baxter-Jr.,-ex-NSA |website=Asia Basket |access-date=June 1, 2025 |date=April 18, 2025}} On April 18, he signed with [[Al Ahly (basketball)|Al Ahly]] of the [[Egyptian Basketball Premier League]].
